## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` needs to lower-case its key before release. Without that, a value set under a mixed-case key can't be read back, which breaks the case-insensitive key rule that the class documents.

## Changes
This pull request adds a `Cache.set` method and raises `DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds, with the comment updated to match. It also adds tests for the set/get round trip, the default TTL value and expiry.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `c.set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `c.get("Alpha")` returns `None`, because `set` stores the raw `"Alpha"` key while `get` looks up `key.lower()`. The comment at `app/cache.py:14-15` says "every path into _store lower-cases the key first". `test_set_then_get_round_trip` only sets the lowercase `"alpha"`, so it passes despite the bug. — Any caller that sets a mixed-case key never gets a cache hit, and the entry stays in `_store` because `get` never finds it to evict. — Fix: Use `self._store[key.lower()] = ...` and extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip` with a mixed-case `set` call.
